Despite today’s reasonably crunchy Friday, it’s as good a day as any to share my test of the “Great Easening” Hypothesis. Many longtime solvers had asserted that Friday and Saturday crosswords have gotten easier, but I (having solved only since 2023) hadn’t observed it, and wondered how much “easening” was real and how much stemmed from solvers’ improving skill or the toughest puzzles being more memorable. So this summer I completed all the Fridays and Saturdays from the first 22 weeks of 2016 (Jan-May). I then compared my times to the first 22 weeks of 2026: 88 puzzles total, same solver roughly contemporaneously.

Bottom line: My doubts are gone. The Easening is more dramatic than I expected. Both the Friday and Saturday puzzles from 2016 took me about 66% longer on average than their 2026 counterparts.  My Fri means: 26:35 for 2016, 16:01 for 2026. Sat means: 39:16 for 2016, 23:43 for 2026.  Fri medians: 22:28 for 2016, 13:43 for 2026. Sat medians: 36:11 for 2016, 19:48 for 2026 (an 82% difference!). There was lots of noise, with some easy puzzles in 2016 (e.g., an 11-min Friday) and some hard ones in 2026 (Fri/Sat max both ~50 min). But the shift was similar across the whole distribution: the easiest puzzles are easier now, the hardest puzzles less hard, etc. 2026’s Saturdays were slightly easier than 2016’s Fridays.

Of course, I’m one person--try it yourself! Whether the change is bad is a different question. I’ll add a reply below re my qualitative experience.

Wordplay such as [Act like yourself, perhaps?] for DO A CAMEO, [Element of a dating profile?], for TREE RING, [Clicked with a partner?] for TAP DANCED -- three sublime original clues.   

Wordplay makes the brain work in a feel-good way, and often makes it belly-laugh.  You’re not just cracking riddles, but you’re having a good time as well. To me, that’s crosswords at its best.  

Throw in freshness like NYT debuts, SNIFF TEST, I GOT IN, and DO A CAMEO, and that's crosswords at its very best.
